text.p: The following are the stories reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Small and medium businesses in Kaunas accused big bussiness representatives, police and tax inspection of the city of deliberately hurting their activities.
- European Union comissioner Hans Van den Broek starts his two-day visit to Lithuania on Wednesday to get acquaintaned with the country's preparations for the memebership in EU.
- State-owned Birzai Naftotiekis pipeline group had a 33.5 million litas net profit and decided to pay 1.5 litas in dividends for a share with face value of 10 litas.
- Vilnius and Hermis banks, Rokishkio Cheese and Medienos Plaushas companies are to were included into the official trading list of Vilnius bourse on Tuesday.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Tuesday he believed that the eastern boarder of the country will be the boarder of European Union in the future.
- Brazauskas appointed on Tuesday a retired U.S. officer Algimantas Garsys as inspector general of the country's forces.
- After repaying its debts to Russia's Gazprom, Lithuanian Gas will not take any more loans from foreign banks before next winter.
- Lithuania's foreign policy coordination council said on Tuesday that the priority aims of the country are full membership in European Union and NATO.
- Austrian Creditanstalt Investment Bank AG eyes the Lithuanian market and is interested in participating in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom.
- Bank Snoras reported its net profit of 16.1 million litas in 1996 and will pay 30 percent in dividends.
- Lietuvos Energija reported 131.8 million litas losses in 1996 and will not pay dividends.
- Mazeikiu Nafta oil refinery, which had 17.8 million litas losses in 1996, plans a profit for 1997.
